newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Thai deals in the making.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Thai deals in the making.

text.p: Asian debt markets served a mixed menu on Wednesday but news of Thai issues provided the main course.
Some details were out on upcoming issues for Siam City Bank and Thai Danu Bank.
Siam City Bank plans to launch a US$100 million floating rate certificates of deposit issue next week
Chase Manhattan Asia is arranger and bookrunner. Other arrangers are Asahi Finance Hongkong, Dresdner (Southeast Asia) and Berliner Bank.
The certificates have a tenor of three years and are expected to pay an all-in return of 67 basis points.
That's much more than the 53.3 basis points Siam City paid for its floating rate note issue launched in January 1996, which had a maturity of five years and a put after three.
But that note now is trading on the wide side, insofar as it is trading at all, secondary market sources said. Traders said that bond was indicated around 80 basis points over LIBOR.
"The offer has widened, but people don't want to make a loss so investors aren't doing anything," said one trader.
Thai Danu Bank's one-year paper is pegged at around 70 basis points, while its paper due in 1999 is loosely indicatd on either side of 90 basis points.
Those issues also are seeing little activity, traders said.
Thai Danu's new issue is a US$150 million floating rate certificate of deposit, bankers said. DBS Bank and Societe Generale Asia are the arrangers.
The facility has two tranches.

Tranche A of US$100 million has a final maturity of five years with put and a call options in year three. It pays a coupon of 60 basis points over LIBOR and an all-in in the low 80s, according to bankers.
Tranche B of US$50 million has a final maturity of five years with annual put options. It pays a coupon of 40 basis points and an all-in in the low 50s.
Bankers said worries about Thailand's economy and the recent attacks on the baht have unnerved investors, putting pressure on the outstanding issues of some of the country's banks.
The top tier banks have not been as badly affected, however.
For example, top-rated Thai Farmers Bank recently managed to put together a US$125 million five-year FRCD that paid 27 basis points all-in.
And Bangkok Bank's outstanding five-year FRCD, which raised eyebrows when it was launched last August at a tight 24 basis points all-in, is indicated on either side of 30 basis points, traders said.
The Kingdom of Thailand announced last week that it would launch its debut Yankee bond, a US$500 million issue with a tenor of 10 to 30 years.

In other news, Citra Marga Finance BV, a special purpose vehicle of Citra Marga Nusaphala, has launched a US$125 million five-year 144a bond that will be priced to yield 130-135 basis points over comparable Treasuries.
Peregrine Fixed Income is lead manager along with SBC Warburg and Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette.
Belle Corp has mandated Deutsche Morgan Grenfell to arrange a five-year US$100 million FRN. Roadshows will be held in late February.
